question:
**Agricultural Production Planning Case Study**

A region's crop yields depend on three fertilizers: $F_1$, $F_2$, $F_3$. The crop response (in quintals per hectare) is given by:

$A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$

The total desired yields are

$Y = \begin{bmatrix}20 \\ 22 \\ 30\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Formulate a linear system to determine the fertilizer allocation.

(b) Use properties of the determinant to decide if unique solutions exist.

(c) Find the inverse of $A$ and solve for the fertilizer vector.
explanation:
(a)
Let $X = \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3\end{bmatrix}$ represent the amounts of $F_1$, $F_2$, $F_3$.
System: $AX=Y$.

(b)
Compute determinant:
$|A| = 1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} - 2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix} + 1\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$
$= 1(1\times3 - 1\times2) - 2(2\times3 - 1\times2) + 1(2\times1 - 1\times1)$
$= 1(3-2) - 2(6-2) + 1(2-1)$
$= 1 - 8 + 1 = -6$
Thus $|A| \neq 0$ so a unique solution exists.

(c)
Find $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{-6}(\text{adj}A)$.
Compute cofactors, form adjugate matrix, and multiply with $Y$.
This gives the fertilizer allocation vector.

options.A:
(a) $AX=Y$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&1\\2&1&2\\1&1&3\end{bmatrix}$ and $Y=\begin{bmatrix}20\\22\\30\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=0$, so no unique solution exists.
(c) The inverse of $A$ does not exist.
options.B:
(a) $AX=Y$, where $X=\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=-6\ne0$, so a unique solution exists.
(c) $A^{-1}=-\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}1&-5&3\\-4&2&0\\1&1&-3\end{bmatrix}$ and $X=\begin{bmatrix}0\\6\\8\end{bmatrix}$.
options.C:
(a) $AX=Y$, where $X=\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\\x_3\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) $|A|=6\ne0$, so a unique solution exists.
(c) $X=\begin{bmatrix}6\\0\\8\end{bmatrix}$.
options.D:
(a) $YA=X$.
(b) $|A|=-6\ne0$, but the system is inconsistent.
(c) No fertilizer allocation is possible.
